title: Model Watchtower: Continuity Playbook & Competitive-Signal Integration Sprint
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational 'Model Watchtower' playbook and a short integration sprint to fold competitive and market signals into the model-continuity dashboard. Deliverables: 1) a continuity scoring model that synthesizes availability, latency variance, and signal-derived substitution risk; 2) signal ingestion spec and lightweight pipeline prototype; 3) dashboard panels and alert rules for SRE/Customer Success; 4) a runbook for procurement & PM handoffs when substitution risk exceeds thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Continuity score prototype runs on daily snapshot and matches expected risk buckets for 5 sample models; 2) Ingestion pipeline ingests 3 signal sources (provider availability, pricing pulses, and model release cadence) into a canonical signal table; 3) Dashboard contains continuity score, top-3 substitution drivers, and alerting rule tested end-to-end with a synthetic incident; 4) Runbook with clear remediation steps, stakeholders and SLAs published to Confluence and linked from dashboard.
updates: 2026-02-20 — Triage: scoped by Aisha. Core hypothesis: blending external market signals with internal telemetry reduces blind substitution risk and gives earlier procurement triggers.

2026-02-24 — PM kickoff meeting with Eng (Miguel), Research (Juno Park), and SRE (Priya Singh). Agreed MVP boundary: do not alter serving runtime; focus on signal fusion and ops tooling first. Action: Eng to prototype signal schema; Research to propose weighting heuristics.

2026-02-28 — Research note (Juno) uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ModelWatchtowerResearch. Preliminary weighting: availability(40%), latency-variance(25%), release-cadence(15%), pricing-shock(20%). Flag: need to validate weights against historical outages.

2026-03-04 — Eng design doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Model+Watchtower+Spec. Schema chosen: flat canonical_signal table with fields: model_id, signal_type, value, timestamp, provenance. Decided to use incremental ingestion via Kafka topic 'model-signals-v2'.

2026-03-07 — Trade-off discussion: realtime (complex, higher cost) vs daily-batched (cheaper, slower). Decision: implement daily-batched MVP with 1-hour near-realtime lift for provider-availability only. Recorded rationale in design doc.

2026-03-09 — Eng prototype complete: noise-filter step added to squash transient provider blips. Github PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/signal-pipeline/pull/223. Requesting Eng review and SRE sign-off on alert noise profile.
2026-03-11 — SRE review (Priya): requested backoff tightening and test harness for synthetic flapping. Miguel assigned to add test harness and update alerts to include hysteresis windows.

2026-03-12 — PM review (Aisha): added acceptance criteria and clarified procurement handoff steps. Request from Sales: include latency-sensitive customer mapping to continuity score for prioritization.

2026-03-14 — Dashboard mockups uploaded by Design (Eleni): https://drive.google.com/file/d/ModelWatchtowerMockups. Panels: continuity heatmap, model timeline, top substitution drivers, affected-customer list. Design feedback: make top drivers actionable (link to PRD and runbook items).

2026-03-15 — Demo to SRE and CS: ran synthetic outage for a regionally-constrained model. Continuity score dropped to 'High' and fired the channel alert. Observations: noisy when provider availability toggles rapidly; need to tune smoothing window.

2026-03-16 — Next steps assigned: 1) Miguel to land PR and add test harness (ETA 2026-03-22); 2) Research to run backtest of weighting on last 6 months (ETA 2026-03-25); 3) Design to finalize dashboard copy and exportable CSV (ETA 2026-03-20); 4) PM to draft runbook and stakeholder contact matrix (Aisha, ETA 2026-03-24).
notes: Risk: noisy external signals could generate alert fatigue. Mitigations: conservative hysteresis, only alert when continuity score sustained above threshold for N minutes, and attach a short confidence vector to each alert. Long-term: consider runtime probes and automated fallback rollouts integrated with Dedicated capacity planners.
